Purpose And Status

Copyable briefs and an illustrative example for applying UX And Screen Design Standards.

Status: template, with a worked example.

Operating Context

Production-oriented web application screens, CRUD tasks and registration journeys. The depth of the record should match the consequence and uncertainty of the change.

Standards Demonstrated

  • Journeys and Decisions
  • Forms and Data Entry
  • Feedback and Recovery
  • Accessibility
  • Evaluation and Validation

Prerequisites And Inputs

Identify the task, audience, approved business rules and existing component conventions. Replace placeholders and label unknowns. Store the result within the feature specification or link it from the existing issue; avoid a parallel document that can drift from implemented behavior.

Secret And Data Handling

Use synthetic people and records. Do not place customer data, credentials or unnecessary research identifiers in a public brief or screenshot. No runtime credentials are needed for these Markdown artifacts.

Validation

Check the brief against the actual interface and UX Checklist. Record checks performed, observed behavior, unresolved assumptions and remaining issues. Template completion is not evidence that a user can complete the task.

Operational Limitations And Lifecycle

The example defines hypothetical business rules; do not copy its required fields, duplicate policy or archive semantics without checking the product. It is not executable UI or tested usability evidence. The feature owner should review the brief when task, audience, components or server behavior changes.

Files

File Purpose
Screen and Journey Brief Copyable task, field, action, state and validation contract
Customer Registration Example Worked application to create, edit and archive a customer record

References

UX References And Adoption Notes distinguish source guidance from the local conventions illustrated here.
